why: Variable window, the shortest valid: a window is good once it holds at least k distinct values. Grow the right end; while the window is still good, record its length and shrink from the left; the smallest length recorded is the answer.
hints: For a fixed right end, if [left, right] is good, are longer windows ending at right also good?
Yes, so for each right you want the largest left that keeps it good. Keep a value -> count map and the number of distinct values.
For each right: add arr[right]; while distinct >= k, best = min(best, right - left + 1), then remove arr[left] and left += 1. Return -1 if best was never set. O(n).
pitfalls: Record the length BEFORE shrinking past validity, inside the while loop.
If the whole array has fewer than k distinct values, return -1.
Decrement distinct only when a count drops to 0.
